chunks: 3670 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

“A woman has no authority, alongside her husband, regarding emancipation, charity, tadbir, gift, or vow concerning her wealth, except with her husband’s permission, except in zakat, kindness to her parents, or maintaining ties with her relatives.”

key_terms.بِرِّ وَالِدَيْهَا: kindness and dutiful conduct toward her parents
key_terms.تَدْبِيرٍ: a form of posthumous manumission arrangement
key_terms.زَكَاةٍ: obligatory alms-tax exempted here from needing permission
key_terms.نَذْرٍ: a vowed act involving one’s wealth

ai.seo_question: What financial actions may a married woman undertake without her husband’s permission according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a married woman’s financial dispositions in certain categories of transactions and vows in relation to her husband’s permission. It also identifies exceptions, namely zakat, dutifulness to parents, and maintaining kinship ties.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3670 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (as), who said:

"A woman has no authority with her husband regarding emancipation, charity, endowment, gift, or vow concerning her wealth, except with her husband's permission-except in the case of Zakat, kindness to her parents, or maintaining ties with her relatives."
